messages:
mari: Heads up — p95 for /chat/streaming started drifting up after the token-throttler change on canary this morning. Seeing ~40ms increase on tier:gold routes. any quick wins? :eyes:

jonathan: saw that in traces. root cause looks like throttler is cutting token budgets earlier for routes with high kv-miss ratio. those requests then fall into smaller microbatches which kills kernel ampf.

sylvie: interesting — could be interaction between budget cutoff and kernel selection heuristics. if batch size drops below kernel-optimized minibatch, we switch kernels and incur extra 10–30ms.

kevin: can you paste a sample trace? also kv hit rate on affected routes?

mari: sure. snippet from the debug trace: 
```
route: /chat/streaming
tier: gold
kv_hit_rate: 0.42
microbatch: 2 -> kernel switch: aten_fused -> fallback_gemm
p95_latency_before: 210ms
p95_latency_after: 250ms
throttler_token_target: 18 -> enforced 12
```

jonathan: thanks. looks like the throttler target reduction + kv churn reduces effective tokens/call and our batching fabric ends up with many tiny minibatches. kernel selection logic picks a safer gemm path which is slower for these sequence lengths.

sylvie: rough plan: 1) make throttler kv-aware (bonus tokens for routes with low kv hits), 2) add hysteresis to kernel selector to avoid flipping on tiny batch size changes, 3) run perf canary with staged split.

kevin: aggro test idea: keep token target lower but artificially pad requests at router to preserve minibatch size for kernels. if padding recovers latency, kernel flip is primary. we should avoid padding in prod long-term.

perf-bot: perf/regression detected: p95 +40ms for route:/chat/streaming on canary pool-7 at 3478898000. Link: https://ci.redwood/perf/3478898000

mari: I ran a quick microprofile comparing two flows. summary: when minibatch <=3, aten_fused fallback frequently, throughput down, p95 up. when minibatch >=6, fused path chosen and p95 improves by ~30ms.

jonathan: sounds like we need a token-budget floor per minibatch threshold. e.g., ensure throttler never reduces expected tokens/call below X if predicted batch size < Y. heuristics can use moving avg batch size + kv_hit_rate.

kevin: let's not hardcode X/Y; propose an adaptive gating function:
```
if predicted_minibatch < 4 and kv_hit_rate < 0.6:
  increment token_budget by ceil( (4 - predicted_minibatch) * 2 )
```
We can canary that.

sylvie: also add a small kernel-selection hysteresis: require two consecutive microbatch-size drops before switching kernel. reduces flip-flop.

mari: can we roll a quick canary with these three changes (kv-aware top-up, gating, hysteresis) to pool-7? i'd like logs and kernel decision traces.

jonathan: I'll draft the canary config. plan: 1% traffic to pool-7, circuit-breaker, collect kernel_decision_metric, kv_hit_rate, batch_size_hist, per-route p95. two-hour window. revert automated if p95 regressed >10ms.

kevin: I'll add padded-minibatch experiment as a short A/B: group A pad, group B apply kv top-up. compare.

mari: temporary mitigation idea: if route tier==gold, prefer keeping token_budget bias +5 tokens until we finish canary. low risk for now and buys us breathing room. thoughts? :thinking_face:

jonathan: acceptable as short-term opt-in. add feature-flag and kill switch. ops should be able to toggle per-route.

perf-bot: experiment scheduled: canary 3478910000 (1% traffic) with tags [kv-topup, kernel-hysteresis, padded-ab]. Will auto-collect metrics.

mari: action items: jonathan - canary config + feature-flag by EOD, kevin - padded AB experiment code + baselines, sylvie - kernel hysteresis impl + unit tests, i'll monitor p95 and kv metrics and post updates in this thread.

kevin: noted. i'll also capture microbench kernels perf diff at seq=128/256 and share numbers.

jonathan: quick note — we should watch for cost impact of adding tokens back. Redwood Optimize should show unit econ; don't want unexpected spend. set a cost alert.

mari: added cost alert to canary dashboard. threshold: +8% token cost over baseline -> auto scale back.

deploy-bot: canary started 3478910000 | target pool pool-7 | experiments: kv-topup,kernel-hysteresis,padded-ab

sylvie: if canary passes, next step is a phased rollout with decayed token top-up: 100% gold-> +5 tokens, 50% silver-> +3 tokens for 24h, monitor.

mari: thanks all. i'll report back after two-hour window. :thumbsup:
